get_delegation.description: See which name servers the parent zone (.com for example.com) sends people to for a domain, with their addresses, and its DS records, which show whether DNSSEC is switched on at the registry.

parameters.description: The domain to test, such as example.com. A web address or an email address works too: only the domain is used.

dnssec.description: True when the parent zone holds DS records for the domain.

ds_records.description: The DS records. Empty without DNSSEC.

items.description: A DS record: the parent zone's fingerprint of one of the domain's DNSSEC keys.

algorithm.description: The key's algorithm number, e.g. 13 for ECDSA P-256.

digest_type.description: How the fingerprint was made: 2 is SHA-256.

key_tag.description: The key's tag, a number that identifies it.

found.description: True when the parent zone lists name servers for the domain. False usually means the domain is not registered.

name_server_names.description: The name servers' host names, each once.

name_servers.description: Each name server address, one entry per address.

items.description: A name server and one of its addresses.

ip.description: One of its IP addresses, IPv4 or IPv6. Empty if not given.

name.description: The name server's host name, e.g. 'ns1.example.com'.

test_domain.description: Check a domain's DNS health with Zonemaster and wait for the verdict: whether its name servers answer and agree, can be reached over IPv4 and IPv6, and whether DNSSEC is set up right. Returns ok, warning, error or critical, the problems found and a link to the full report. A test usually takes under a minute; if it takes over 4 minutes the step returns the test id so 'Get test results' can pick it up.
